Subject: Post-demo: Decision pathway & contract signer velocities

Thanks again for taking the time today, Ari — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Key takeaways from the demo:
- Use case: secure customer support summaries + indexed retrieval (low PII exposure).
- Primary success metrics: 50% reduction in average handle time, <200ms median inference latency on standard tickets.
- Pilot ask: 4-week pilot with 5k monthly ticket volume, isolated workspace.

Stakeholder map (please confirm):
- Economic buyer: Taylor Grant (CFO) — controls procurement & final sign-off.
- Security / InfoSec reviewer: Manish Rao (you mentioned).
- Procurement: Taylor but procurement team will own vendor comparisons.

Contracting / legal sequencing we recommend:
1) Mutual NDA to enable deeper security docs exchange (SOC2, architecture diagrams).
2) DPA if pilot processes regulated data (we can draft standard language).
3) MSA for pilot + production terms.

Suggested cadence / turn-times (flexible):
- NDA: 5 business days turn (redline sprint).
- DPA (if needed): 7–10 business days.
- MSA: 2–4 weeks depending on redlines.

Attachments: Demo-recording.mp4 (recording), Initial-MAP.xlsx (draft mutual action plan).

Immediate asks:
- Ari: confirm stakeholder contacts and who will own signatures for NDA vs MSA.
- Ari: confirm any non-standard legal terms we should expect (IP carve-outs, data residency, indemnity caps).

Ben & Rishi: I’ve looped you to own pricing cadence and technical follow-ups respectively. Evelyn, please standby for security questionnaire request — sending SOC2 next after Ari confirms.

Thanks — aiming to have NDA out by Friday if we get stakeholder confirmations today.

—

Hi Vanessa — great session, appreciate the clarity. Confirming stakeholders and a few notes below.

Stakeholders:
- Economic buyer / Procurement: Taylor Grant (CFO) — will own vendor comparisons and signature.

Timing constraints and considerations:
- Procurement is doing a formal vendor shortlist; they expect to close shortlist in ~3 weeks. Speed here helps.
- Security will need an architecture diagram and the SOC2 report; they prefer redacting customer lists on SOC2.
- Legal typically requires NDA in place before sharing full tech docs.

Contract preferences:
- NDA first; then technical exchange; MSA after pilot.
- We usually ask for modest limits on indemnity for pilots and a 60-day notice for data deletion on pilot end.

Attachments: CuraLogic_SOC2_redacted.pdf (redacted version).

Thanks — jumping in on contracting cadence. I'll own shepherding legal and pricing through the redline window. Proposed approach:

1) NDA (DocuSign): we will send our standard mutual NDA with a 5 business day review expectation. If Cur aLogic needs changes, our legal ops will triage and batch small asks to minimize ping-pong.
2) DPA (if needed): we can provide a templated DPA; Evelyn, please add any security notes for PII handling.
3) MSA: target a 2–3 week redline sprint post-NDA for initial pilot MSA (assuming no material indemnity/data residency asks). For more complex indemnities we should expect 3–6 weeks.

Turn-time owners:
- NDA: Redwood legal ops (Ben) — initial send by EOD 6/22, target signature 6/26.
- Security docs: Evelyn — provide architecture + answers within 3 business days after NDA signature.
- Pricing / commercial: Vanessa & Ben — provide pricing-sheet v2 by 6/23.

Operational notes:
- We prefer redlines in a single Google Doc (version controlled) and DocuSign for the signature step.
- If Cur aLogic wants us to accept a counterparty template, we’ll need to scope the open issues up front and propose a mediation path.

Attachment: Pricing-template-v2.xlsx (pricing + commercial options).
